records.title: The Critique of Pure Reason
records.author: Immanuel Kant
records.edition_verification: Title and translator inspected on fetched title page. Page includes prefaces headed 1781 and 1787 and the B-style Deduction. Underlying print impression/date not established from this page; no German collation. Do not substitute this translation’s section numbers for conventional B-Deduction numbering.
records.reading_scope: Selected passages only; not the complete work.

inspected_passages.locator: First Part, Transcendental Æsthetic, §§1–7
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: We maintain, therefore, the empirical reality of space
supports: PH-K01: space and time as forms of sensibility; empirical reality and transcendental ideality
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Quotation is a fragment of §4, followed in source by qualification to possible external experience.

inspected_passages.locator: Transcendental Æsthetic, §9, opening and rainbow discussion
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: we should not thereby advance one step nearer
supports: PH-K01/03: increased empirical clarity does not reach things in themselves; empirical appearance/reality distinction differs from transcendental distinction
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Selected opening only, not entire section. The fragment concerns higher clarity of empirical intuition.

inspected_passages.locator: Analytic of Conceptions, Chapter I, Section III, Table of the Categories
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: Of Causality and Dependence (cause and effect)
supports: PH-K02: four headings of categories and category of causality

inspected_passages.locator: Chapter II, Section I, Of the Principles of a Transcendental Deduction in general, §9
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: does not concern itself with the right, but only with the fact
supports: PH-K02: transcendental justification differs from empirical origin

inspected_passages.locator: Chapter II, Section II, §§11–18, conjunction through legitimate cognitive use
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: To think an object and to cognize an object are by no means the same thing.
supports: PH-K02: synthesis, apperception, judgment, objective unity, category use
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: The §12 wording “must accompany” is compared with Rohlf’s quoted “must be able to accompany”; no German wording verified.

inspected_passages.locator: Transcendental Deduction, §22 and Result §23, selected passages
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: Particular laws, inasmuch as they concern empirically determined phenomena, cannot be entirely deduced from pure laws
supports: PH-K02: categories condition possible experience without supplying particular empirical laws
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Selected passages, not claimed complete reading of all intervening text or full Deduction.

inspected_passages.locator: Analytic of Principles, Analogies of Experience, B. SECOND ANALOGY; house and ship examples
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: Principle of the Succession of Time According to the Law of Causality.
supports: PH-K02: apprehension order versus objective event order; causal rule
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Beginning and selected proof paragraphs, not entire Second Analogy.

inspected_passages.locator: Chapter III, Of the Ground of the Division of all Objects into Phenomena and Noumena
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: this is a noumenon in the negative sense of the word.
supports: PH-K03: negative and positive noumenon; logical consistency versus real possibility; boundary concept
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Substantial chapter opening through negative/positive distinction and limitation, not all subsequent material.

inspected_passages.locator: Transcendental Dialectic, Introduction I and II A–C, selected passages
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: Transcendental illusion, on the contrary, does not cease to exist
supports: PH-K04: persistence of transcendental illusion; reason’s demand for unconditioned
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Excerpt distinguishes illusion from an ordinary removable logical mistake.

inspected_passages.locator: Antithetic of Pure Reason, FIRST CONFLICT and SECOND CONFLICT, proofs and initial observations
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: The world has a beginning in time, and is also limited in regard to space.
supports: PH-K04: first two antinomies and their arguments
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: This is thesis asserted within an antinomy, not a doctrine to attribute without its antithesis and resolution.

inspected_passages.locator: Antinomy, Section VII Critical Solution; Section VIII Regulative Principle
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: If that which is conditioned is given, the whole series of its conditions is also given
supports: PH-K04: criticized cosmological inference; condition as task rather than completed totality
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Quoted proposition is the dialectical inference Kant criticizes, not an endorsed inference.

inspected_passages.locator: Appendix, Of the Regulative Employment of the Ideas of Pure Reason, opening
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: regulative ideas, directing the understanding to a certain aim
supports: PH-K04: constructive role for inquiry and unity
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Selected opening, not the full Appendix.

verification_limits: No full A/B pagination in Gutenberg source used as authority.
No direct primary reading of all third/fourth antinomy arguments; contrast relies on K-SEP-META.
Public-domain English translation may obscure distinctions; contemporary dialogue must not inherit its register.

inspected_passages.locator: Selected §2 theory of illusion discussion

supports: PH-K04: diagnosis of illusion and positive role of reason

inspected_passages.locator: §4 The World and Rational Cosmology; §§4.1–4.2

inspected_passages.locator: Opening and §1.1 Transcendental Realism and Empirical Idealism
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: there is so little consensus
supports: PH-K01/03: contested interpretation
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Also inspected §1.1 discussion at extracted lines 230–337; quotation fragment belongs to introductory discussion of disagreement.

inspected_passages.locator: §1.1 Transcendental Realism and Empirical Idealism
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: Transcendental idealism is a form of empirical realism
supports: PH-K01: distinction from empirical idealism

inspected_passages.locator: Selected §3.4.3 affection discussion through §4.1
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: two different perspectives or stances
supports: PH-K03: affection problem and dual-aspect alternative
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: This is Stang’s account of a family of interpretations, not a settled equation of Kant’s doctrine with it.

inspected_passages.locator: Selected §4.3 objections, especially §4.3.3 Abstraction
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: merely refrain from representing them
supports: PH-K01/03: abstracting a predicate differs from asserting its negation
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Selected spans read at 1966–2020 and 2082–2155; intervening text not claimed inspected.

inspected_passages.locator: §4.4 and selected §4.5 objections to Langton
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: substances with intrinsic properties
supports: PH-K03: metaphysical dual-aspect reading and textual objections
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Langton’s book not directly inspected; do not cite it as read.

inspected_passages.locator: §6 introduction and §6.1 Phenomena and noumena
inspected_passages.short_excerpt_actually_inspected: the noumenon in a positive sense
supports: PH-K03: conceptual distinction and B307 quoted definition
inspected_passages.limits_or_notes: Verified secondary A/B locators from quotations: A20/B34, A249, A251–252, B307. These are not independently collated to paginated German.
